summary:
SMS Posen was one of the first dreadnoughts built for the German Imperial Navy. Commissioned in 1910, the Nassau-class battleship carried twelve 28 cm guns in six twin turrets.

During World War I, Posen served mainly in the North Sea and took part in several fleet operations. At the Battle of Jutland in May 1916, she fought British ships and accidentally rammed the German light cruiser Elbing, which was later scuttled. Posen also supported German operations against Russia in the Gulf of Riga and returned to the Baltic in 1918 to support White Finnish forces during the Finnish Civil War.

After the war, Posen remained in Germany while most of the German fleet was interned at Scapa Flow. Britain received her in 1919 as a replacement for ships scuttled there. She was scrapped in the Netherlands in 1922.
